messages:
tanya: Hey, backup restore for tenant-88 failed during decrypt. Error: "AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to use the key "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"". We ran an RBAC cleanup earlier today — could that have pruned something?

mike: Which bucket/snapshot and any full error lines? If the KMS grant for the uploader SA was removed, restores will fail with that exact error.

tanya: Bucket: s3://redwood-backups-prod/tenant-88/2026-03-21/tenant-88-snap.tar.gz
Log snippet: ```
2026-03-21T09:12:03Z restore-service ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to use the key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01
    at com.amazon.kms.client.Decrypt(Decrypt.java:45)
```

ana? (typo fixed) ana: fwiw we rotated the backup-uploader service account last night. PR #3421 removed the legacy `backup-uploader` role and replaced it with `backup-uploader-v2` — did we re-grant KMS access to the new principal?

leo: Quick check: list grants for the CMK in question. Example CLI: ```
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 | jq '.Grants[] | {granteePrincipal,operations}'
```

(tanya runs it) tanya: output shows only AWSAccount"111122223333" and a lambda principal — no `backup-uploader-v2` grants present. Snippet: ```
{
  "granteePrincipal": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/legacy-backup-handler",
  "operations": ["Encrypt"]
}
```

jason: Security question: did the policy-enforcer job run as part of the RBAC cleanup? CloudTrail should show a RevokeGrant or DisableKeyPolicy change if someone touched KMS. Try: ```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=RevokeGrant --start-time 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-21T12:00:00Z
```

audit-bot: policy-enforcer v2: automated action at 2026-03-21T03:05:11Z — removed IAM role binding `backup-uploader` from `infra:backup-group` due to stale org membership. Rule: orphaned-role-prune v1.2. (ticket #INC-7342)

mike: OK mitigation path: 1) re-create a KMS grant for the new principal, 2) do a canary restore in staging, 3) add detection + a guardrail in policy-enforcer. Example create-grant CLI: ```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 \  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/backup-uploader-v2 \  --operations Decrypt Encrypt ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo GenerateDataKey
```
Note: grants are ephemeral by default — use `--name` and track the GrantId in ticket.

ana? ana: please test in staging first. Also add a Splunk rule to alert on `kms:Decrypt` AccessDenied or `KMS_DecryptDenied` CloudTrail events. Splunk query example: ```
index=cloudtrail eventName=Decrypt errorCode=AccessDenied* | stats count by userIdentity.principalId, eventTime, requestParameters.keyId
```

tanya: I'll run the create-grant in staging and validate restores. tagging @mike and @jason as reviewers. I'll also pin this thread and create an incident ticket for a full postmortem and timeline.

jason: Action items: (a) immediate grant recreation in staging+prod (tanya/mike), (b) add a detection alert (ana), (c) update policy-enforcer to skip pruning roles with active KMS grants (eng-infra + security), (d) postmortem documenting the RBAC change -> KMS grant gap and a follow-up on automation. Assigning owners in #incidents. :thumbsup:
